skill_entry.name: 9. Passages a later reader cannot use: PR-body sections, code comments and Notes
skill_entry.trigger: Part A (unchanged): the PR body has a Status, Verification, Tests or Results section; the body procedure runs only inside those sections. Part B, on the diff under h/, src/ or t/, any one: (B1) an added comment line carries a review label (class R: 'PR <n> review|round|comment', 'review round', 'round <n>', 'comment W<n>', 'R<n>-M<n>', 'as discussed with') in any of the three trees, or a tracker id (class T: Story or STORY-<n>, ticket <n>, JIRA, issue #<n>) under h/ or src/; (B2) an added '// Note [name]' line, at any indentation, followed by the tilde line; (B3) a comment of one to three lines directly above a general-purpose statement (TRACE_EVENT, log call, TRON_ASSERT, counter) that says 'See Note [<a Note this PR adds>]' or names a Note or identifier the PR introduces.
skill_entry.procedure: BASE = merge-base(base.sha from gh api, HEAD); require 0 merges in BASE..HEAD. B1: grep added comment lines, map to HEAD lines, count comments per file (adjacent lines are one comment). Delete the reference: fact still stated = offer that sentence (suggestion block if one line); only history left = ask for what the code guarantees. Class-T hits under t/ are 'also in' lines after an h/ or src/ hit. B2: count comment lines; grep cites outside the file; grep below the tilde line for narrative markers (NaN, crash, wrong, bug, the fix, used to, no longer, the latter put); grep the body for the marker line's parenthesis text. Markers plus body overlap = history whatever the cite count: ask for about five lines at the cited declaration. No marker = keep. B3: git grep every statement token at BASE; all present = justification; ask once per PR to drop the comment and keep the statement. Final head: zero hits, zero cites of a removed Note.
skill_entry.question: Body: if the reviewer could only open GitHub, would deleting this clause change any decision about the head? Code: if a reader in two years had only the code, no GitHub and no tracker, would deleting this comment line, or this whole Note, lose a fact the code must honor, or only the story of who asked for it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A story id or review label in the PR title or a commit subject (PR 2906 '(Story 2814)', PR 4596 '(review round 4, W2)'). A 'See Note [X]' cite of a mechanism Note (13 cites of Note [GOF staging eviction], 2 of Note [Attention path stats]). A long mechanism Note or comment (79-line Note [Attention path stats]; the 12-line inflight_guard comment gof.hpp:105-116 at ffc2d6156a drew only the 'public:' nit). A tracker id in a test file alone (tron-2475 t/t_clearhbm.cpp:47, :83, :150 STORY-397/396 approved silently; the four t/ 'Story 2814' lines of PR 2906 unmarked). A second B3 comment in one PR (src/tron/gof.cpp:89-92 survived to 678f559d5d). A comment longer than three lines above an assert (tron-2875 full.hpp:1656-1661). A TODO with a tracker id. 'ticket 5' as a sequencing token. Prose under doc/. A bare 'see PR #n' pointer: Insufficient data.
skill_entry.finding_shape: Body: unchanged. B1: 'probably don't want to reference "PR <n> review round <k> comment W<x>" like this... seems there are more (<N> comments in <file>). Scrub please.' One-liner: a suggestion block, 'don't mention Story numbers in comments', 'Story <n> frees X' becomes 'X is freed'. B2: 'I'm not sure this (basically) bug-fix is worthy of its own noisy Note. It's not like we are defining some fancy algorithm we need to document; a short comment at <declaration> saying <invariant> is enough.' B3: 'we don't really need this comment IMO... and this <TRACE_EVENT label> really isn't related to Note [<name>] directly. It's a useful event no matter the context.'
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: minor, never blocking: 'probably don't want to', 'we don't really need this comment IMO', 'I'm not sure this ... is worthy', 'Scrub please', 'minor nit'. One comment per file area plus 'seems there are more'; a suggestion block when the fix is one line; one B3 ask per PR. All five members were changed by the author before approval; he approved PR 4596 at the scrubbed head 441e81178b, PR 2906 at ffc2d6156a and PR 4007 at 3a8544cd35.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk (the added comment lines and Note blocks) + full file at HEAD (remaining hits per file, the Note's line count) + other files (git grep for 'Note [name]' cites across h, src, t; git grep of statement tokens at BASE) + PR body (the Why paragraph, to spot a Note that repeats it). Not callers, commits, CI or runtime. The installed positron-code-review skill covers the B1 pattern as a cleanup task; this check adds Wade's severity, the per-file count and the suggestion-block form, and does not replace that skill.

## Common setup (correction, applies to every check)

Replace `BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base $HEAD origin/main)` with:
```
BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base $(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha) $HEAD)
git -C WT log --merges --oneline $BASE..$HEAD | wc -l    # must print 0; otherwise main was merged into the branch and the two-dot diff carries main's comments
```
On a merged PR `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself (PR 4596: 0f784c44ff). base.sha gives 9b60b69dce for PR 4596, merge-base with 0f784c44ff = 66c7bb8db1 = the parent of the first branch commit 9b3832eb4b. Same formula: PR 2906 base.sha f59334dc24 -> ea4be1815a; PR 4007 base.sha 57730b1929 -> 21162f5568. Keep the old formula only when gh is unavailable and the PR is open.

## Check 9: passages a later reader cannot use (PR-body sections, code comments, Notes)

Body part, unchanged (steps 1-5 of the existing section and the "On PR 4557" line). Code part:

6. Reference grep over added comment lines, two classes (awk has no `\b`; keep the pattern free of it; append reviewer logins to PATR if the PR text names them):
```
PATR='(PR ?#?[0-9]{3,5}[ ,]+(review|round|comment)|review round|round [0-9]|comment [WR][0-9]|R[0-9]+-M[0-9]+|as discussed with)'
PATT='([Ss][Tt][Oo][Rr][Yy][ -]?#?[0-9]+|[Tt]icket[ -]?#?[A-Z]*-?[0-9]+|JIRA|issue #[0-9]+)'
git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t | grep -E '^\+\+\+|^@@|^\+' | awk -v pr="$PATR" -v pt="$PATT" '/^\+\+\+/{f=substr($0,7)} /^@@/{split($0,a," "); split(a[3],b,","); n=substr(b[1],2)+0; next} /^\+/{ if ($0 ~ /^\+[ \t]*(\/\/|\*|\/\*)/) { if ($0 ~ pr) print "R " f":"n": "substr($0,2); else if ($0 ~ pt) print "T " f":"n": "substr($0,2) } n++}' | tee c9-hits.txt
awk '{print $1, $2}' c9-hits.txt | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c     # hit LINES per class and file
```
   Count comments, not lines: two printed lines L and L+1 in one file are one comment (a wrapped reference). The ask says "there are more" when a file has more than one comment. Class R fires under h/, src/ and t/. Class T fires under h/ or src/; a class-T hit under t/ is listed as "also in <test file>" after an h/ or src/ hit and is never a finding on its own. A hit whose line also contains `TODO` and sits beside a workaround goes to the workaround check. A line matching only a bare `PR ?#?[0-9]{3,5}` (no review/round/comment word) is not printed; such pointers exist on origin/main (h/libpos.hpp:361, h/tron/generation/harvester.hpp:293, t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:20, t/t_rinzler_tokens.cpp:15604) with no Wade comment either way: Insufficient data, do not post.
7. Reader test per hit: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<L-2>,<L+4>p'`. Delete the reference in your head; if the sentence still carries the fact, propose that sentence as a suggestion block (one-liner) or as the ask. If only the history remains ("the record had two writers"), ask for what the code now guarantees.
8. Note definitions added by the PR (any indentation; the tilde line on the next added line separates a definition from a cite):
```
git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t | grep -E '^\+\+\+|^@@|^\+' | awk '/^\+\+\+/{f=substr($0,7); p=""} /^@@/{split($0,a," "); split(a[3],b,","); n=substr(b[1],2)+0; p=""; next} /^\+/{ line=substr($0,2); if (p ~ /^[ \t]*\/\/ Note \[/ && line ~ /^[ \t]*\/\/ ~~~~/) print f":"n-1": "p; p=line; n++}'
git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | awk -v L=<line> 'NR>=L && /^[ \t]*\/\//{c++} NR>=L && !/^[ \t]*\/\//{print "comment lines " c; exit}'
git -C WT grep -n 'Note \[<name>\]' HEAD -- h src t | grep -v '<defining file>'          # cites outside the file
git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<L+2>,<L+c-1>p' | grep -n -E '\bNaN\b|\bcrash\b|\babort\b|\bwrong\b|\bbug\b|\bthe fix\b|\bbefore the fix\b|\bused to\b|\bno longer\b|\bthe latter put\b'   # narrative markers, below the title and tilde lines
git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<L+2>,<L+c-1>p' | grep -n -E 'qwen|llama|gpt|mixtral|bitfile|first HW pass'   # model or hardware name
gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json body -q .body | grep -c -F '<text inside the parentheses of the marker line, or its first four words after the marker>'   # >0 = the Note repeats the body's Why
```
   Verdict, in this order: (1) a narrative marker is present AND the body repeats the marker line's phrase -> history, whatever the cite count; ask for a comment of about five lines at the declaration the cites point to (the stride function or constant), and the cites become plain references to it. (2) Otherwise keep, whatever the length. A single marker on a mechanism sentence with no body overlap is not history. An outside-file cite does not keep a narrative Note: Note [Fixed KV-head slot geometry] had one (hwattention_dump.hpp:111) and was still trimmed.
9. Feature-link comments of one to three lines above general-purpose statements. FEATURE = the Note names printed by step 8, joined with `|`, plus every backticked identifier and every TRON_* variable in the PR title and the body's first heading; write it in the probe log before running:
```
git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t | grep -E '^\+\+\+|^@@|^\+' | awk -v feat="FEATURE" '/^\+\+\+/{f=substr($0,7); c=""; k=0} /^@@/{split($0,a," "); split(a[3],b,","); n=substr(b[1],2)+0; c=""; k=0; next} /^\+/{ line=substr($0,2); if (line ~ /^[ \t]*\/\//) {c=c "\n" line; k++} else { if (k>=1 && k<=3 && line ~ /(TRACE_EVENT|TRACE_COUNTER|spdlog::|TRON_ASSERT|LOG\(|->inc|fetch_add)/ && c ~ ("See Note \\[|" feat)) print f":"n": lines=" k ": " line c; c=""; k=0 } n++}'
```
   For each print, take every string literal and identifier in the statement line and run `git -C WT grep -c '<token>' BASE -- h src t`. Every token present at BASE = the statement is general-purpose and the comment is a justification (it says what the span brackets or that a cost "is visible"): ask once per PR, on the print whose statement is furthest from the Note, to drop the comment and keep the statement; never ask to remove the statement. A token absent at BASE (new in this PR) = the comment may describe it; keep it and list it only as "same pattern" after a first hit. A comment that states when the event fires and what its number measures is kept (gof.cpp:89-91). A comment longer than three lines is never a B3 hit.
10. Confirm at the final head: step 6 prints nothing; `git -C WT grep -c 'Note \[<removed name>\]' HEAD -- h src t` is 0.

On PR 4596 at HEAD 0f784c44ff (BASE 66c7bb8db1 by the base.sha formula, 0 merges): step 6 prints 6 class-R lines for 5 comments: h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:863 and :864 (one wrapped sentence "... (PR 4596 review round 4, comment W2)"), t/t_attn_stats.cpp:306 (W2), :408 (W4), :662 (W5), t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2227 (W5); hit lines per file 2 / 3 / 1, comments 1 / 3 / 1, so the ask says "there are more" for t_attn_stats.cpp. Wade marked attn_stats.hpp:863 (4146947611) and t_attn_stats.cpp:306 (4146959502, "seems there are more. Scrub please."). Step 7: every sentence keeps its fact with the reference deleted. Step 8: one definition, attn_stats.hpp:6 Note [Attention path stats], 79 comment lines (6-84), 2 cites outside the file (both h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:470 and :800), 0 narrative markers with the step-8 pattern (the old pattern's "was " matched line 14 "was copied once per apply_page_range call", a mechanism sentence) -> kept; Wade did not comment on it. Step 9 with FEATURE 'Attention path stats|TRON_ATTN_STATS|attn_stats': no print. Step 10 at 441e81178b (commit "Attention path stats: comments without review history, one row-key helper, one fewer test case"): 0 hits; Wade's APPROVED review 5371062950 is at that head.
On PR 2906 at 1c6d3fc8e3 (BASE ea4be1815a, 0 merges): step 6 prints 5 class-T lines: h/pos/hwattention.hpp:134 "Story 2814 frees `data`" (the finding, 3350285744 with a suggestion block) and four t/ lines (t/t_dma_tracker.cpp:438, t/t_gof_dma.cpp:191, :315, t/t_gof_staging_leaks.cpp:1) listed as "also in"; Wade marked only :134; all five are gone at ffc2d6156a (his APPROVED review 4471576292) and at the merged head 678f559d5d, where the Note at hwattention.hpp:130-140 reads "Eviction frees only this host-side formatted copy after every in-flight DMA". Step 8: hwattention.hpp:130 Note [GOF staging eviction], 9 comment lines, 0 markers, 13 cites outside the file (the diff adds 15 "See Note [GOF staging eviction]" lines, 17 lines naming the Note in any form) -> kept. Step 9 with FEATURE 'GOF staging eviction' prints two 3-line hits: h/tron/models/model.hpp:1881 TRACE_EVENT("hwattention", "gof_rodeo", "layer", layer) under the comment at :1878-1880 (gof_rodeo present at BASE in 8 files, so a justification: Wade's 3350412400; at 678f559d5d the TRACE_EVENT stands at :1904 with no comment), and src/tron/gof.cpp:92 TRACE_EVENT("hwattention", "gof_populate", "layer", layer) under a comment ending "See Note [GOF staging eviction]" (gof_populate absent at BASE; the comment says when it fires and what the slices measure; unchanged at ffc2d6156a and 678f559d5d, no Wade comment). The 12-line inflight_guard comment at ffc2d6156a:h/tron/gof.hpp:105-116 drew only "public is redundant" (3391446464 at :118).
On PR 4007 at 29a39ac33e (BASE 21162f5568, 0 merges): step 6 prints nothing. Step 8 prints h/pos/hwattention.hpp:301 Note [Fixed KV-head slot geometry], 13 comment lines (301-313), cites at :464, :988 and h/pos/hwattention_dump.hpp:111; the marker grep below the tilde line prints 2 lines (:310 "the latter put ... wrong", :312 "NaN s_star on the first HW pass of qwen3-30b-a3b"); the model-name grep prints :312; `gh pr view 4007` body grep -c 'NaN s_star' = 1 -> history (3866668853).
